name: SMH
blurb: Shaking my head: shows disappointment, disbelief or disapproval in a text
title: SMH Meaning: What Does SMH Mean in Texting?
description: SMH stands for "shaking my head". It shows disbelief, disappointment or disapproval in texts and comments, often at something silly. Examples.
answer: SMH stands for "shaking my head". It is the written version of slowly shaking your head at something: you use it when you cannot believe what you just read, or you are disappointed or mildly annoyed. It usually goes at the start or end of a message, like "smh, he forgot again". Less often it can mean "scratching my head", for confusion.

body: Cambridge defines SMH as an abbreviation used on social media and in texts when you do not believe something or do not approve of it. The tone is usually tired disappointment rather than anger: think of a parent sighing at a mess. It is a long-established piece of texting shorthand, and "smh my head" became a joke precisely because it repeats the head.

ul: "He put the empty milk carton back in the fridge. Smh."
"Smh, I missed the bus by ten seconds."
"You really thought that was a good idea? SMH."

body: SMH is casual and mostly gentle, good for reacting to small annoyances and silly news. Aimed directly at someone ("smh at you") it reads as judging them, so it can sting in a serious conversation. Skip it at work unless the chat is very relaxed.

faq.a: Shaking my head. Occasionally, scratching my head.
Not by itself. It shows mild disapproval; aimed at someone during an argument it can feel condescending.
A stronger version of SMH that adds a mild swear word for emphasis.
